newsitem.title: INDIA: India wants robust debt market, but will monitor.
newsitem.headline: India wants robust debt market, but will monitor.

text.p: Finance Minister P.Chidambaram said on Thursday that India was keen to create a robust debt market with foreign institutional funds, but said the government would keep watching to ensure control on national debt.
Earlier on Thursday in Bombay, the regulatory Securities and Exchange Board of India (SEBI) allowed foreign institutional investors (FIIs) to invest in government gilts.
SEBI also announced that three foreign debt funds worth $253 million had been approved.
"We have to deepen and widen the debt market," Chidambaram said. "Let us see how we go along. We can always cap it. We can always control it."
"This (foreign portfolio debt) is subject to an overall cap," Chidambaram told a news conference in his New Delhi office. "Each fund comes with a cap."
Chidambaram said foreign institutional debt will be within an overall ceiling the government imposed on external commercial borrowings.
Within this, foreign investment in government securities, or gilts, will be covered by another cap, he said.
